entities.label: TextOfTheConstitution
entities.rationale: The text of the Constitution is a specific information artifact whose content (the linguistic/normative pattern) can be copied and instantiated in multiple physical bearers (parchment, printed copies, digital files). This makes it a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031). It is typed as an instance of the existing working:Statute class, which is already a subclass of BFO_0000031. It is an individual because it refers to a unique, historically identified document content.

relations.rationale: The text of the Constitution is an instance of Statute, a working class already typed as BFO_0000031 (generically dependent continuant), capturing that it is a normative information content that can be multiply instantiated across physical copies.
The text of the Constitution is part of the USConstitution individual already in the ontology; the text is the generically dependent content component of that constitutional document individual.

open_questions: Should 'TextOfTheConstitution' be distinguished from 'USConstitution' (already in the ontology), or is 'USConstitution' already intended to represent the text content? If so, we could simply retype USConstitution as an instance of working:Statute rather than minting a new individual.
Is the intended referent specifically the US Constitution, or a constitution in general? If general, this should be a class rather than an individual.

Should we model a separate individual for a physical copy (a material entity, BFO_0000040) distinct from the text content (BFO_0000031)? This would allow the part-of relation to go from the text (GDC) to the document bearer.
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'the text of the Constitution' refers to a specific information content — the normative linguistic pattern that constitutes the constitutional document. In BFO 2020, such information artifacts are generically dependent continuants (BFO_0000031) because their identity is tied to a reproducible pattern rather than to any particular physical substrate; the same text can be instantiated in many copies. The existing working class 'Statute' (a subclass of BFO_0000031) is the most apt type. Because 'the text of the Constitution' picks out a historically specific document content, it is modeled as an individual (working:TextOfTheConstitution) rather than a class. A part-of relation links it to the already-existing working:USConstitution individual. An open question is raised about whether USConstitution was already intended to play this role, in which case no new individual is needed.
